nodes.name: Fe-Bipy@ZIF Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.36 g Bipy and 0.3 g Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were stirred in methanol for 30 min, after which 2.38 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O was added and the solution was allowed to stir for 1 h more. Another methanol solution of 2.63 g 2-MeIM was added under vigorous stirring, the mixture was then hydrothermally treated under 120 °C for 4 h. Afterwards, collected precipitates (Fe-Bipy@ZIF) were obtained.

nodes.name: Silica Shell Coating
nodes.procedure: Fe-Bipy@ZIF precipitates were coated with a thin silica layer derived from TEOS in H2O and C2H5OH solution containing CTAB and 2-MeIM (TEOS: H2O: C2H5OH: CTAB: 2-MeIM: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O = 1:4093:766:1.5:6.8:0.1, mole ratio).

nodes.name: Confined Pyrolysis Fe-N-C
nodes.procedure: Fe-Bipy@ZIF-8@SiO2 was carbonized in a confined space at 950 °C under inert atmosphere (N2) for 3 h in tubular furnace. The temperature is set at 950 °C and heating rate is 5 °C min⁻¹.

unit_operations.name: Pyrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Fe-N-C was prepared through confined pyrolysis of silica shell protected Fe-Bipy in tubular furnace under N2 for 3 h. The temperature is set at 950 °C and heating rate is 5 °C min⁻¹

nodes.source_text: Finally, Fe-N-C was prepared through confined pyrolysis of silica shell protected Fe-Bipy... under N2 for 3 h

nodes.name: Direct Pyrolysis NPs-N-C
nodes.procedure: The product obtained through direct pyrolysis of Fe-Bipy@ZIF precursor under similar condition (950 °C, 5 °C min⁻¹, N2, 3 h) is named as NPs-N-C.
nodes.source_text: The product obtained through direct pyrolysis of Fe-Bipy@ZIF precursor under similar condition is named as NPs-N-C

nodes.name: EP-n Composite Coatings
nodes.procedure: Homogeneous epoxy resin with Fe-N-C catalyst (0, 0.8, 1.6, 2.4 g·L⁻¹) was deposited on carbon steel by automatic coater to prepare desired coatings. After cured under room temperature for 24 h and 80 °C overnight, the obtained coating named EP-n, n denotes Fe-N-C amount. The thickness of coatings is controlled at 20±2 μm.

nodes.description: ORR performance in oxygen-saturated 0.1 M KOH using RDE
nodes.source_text: The oxygen reduction activity of Fe-N-C was firstly confirmed by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) using a rotating disk electrode (RDE)... Fe-N-C exhibits the best electrochemical activity towards ORR with an onset potential of 1.06 V and a half-wave potential of 0.902 V... limiting current density of 4.78 mA·cm⁻² at 1600 rpm and a kinetic current density of 14.7 mA·cm⁻²... average electron transfer number (n) of Fe-N-C... is 3.9... chronoamperometry plot at 0.5 V, the current density remains 96% after test for 15 h... only 17 mV loss in the half-wave potential... ORR tafel slope of Fe-N-C... is 62 mV·dec⁻¹

nodes.description: EIS anticorrosion performance of EP coatings in oxygen saturated 3.5 wt% NaCl
nodes.source_text: Active anticorrosion performance was studied by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS, Frequency: 10^5 to 10^-2 Hz, sinusoidal voltage: 10 mV.) in oxygen saturated 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The platinum sheet, Ag/AgCl electrode and coated sample served as the counter, reference and working electrode... resistance of EP-0 at 0.01 Hz decreases sharply from 2.79×10^6 to 2.16×10^4 Ω cm²... resistance of composite coatings always remains above 10^7 Ω cm²... EP-0 exhibits the highest oxygen permeability coefficient (3.62×10^-12 cm³·cm/cm²·s·Pa) while the composite coatings... show considerably lower values (1.54×10^-13 to 3.12×10^-13 cm³·cm/cm²·s·Pa)... EP-1.6 shows the lowest water absorption of 2.83%

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k³-weighted EXAFS shows single peak at 1.47 Å; coordination number ~4, Fe-N bond length 1.94 Å confirming tetracoordinated FeN₄ sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier-transformed (FT) k³-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra of Fe-N-C (Fig. 3b), only one prominent peak appears at 1.47 Å... coordination number of the central Fe atom is calculated to be about 4 and the average bond length of Fe-N is 1.94 Å.
